searchText: <milonite> Is there any discussion ongoing re refills for selfdestruct? As long as same-tx `SELFDESTRUCT` stays in the EVM (and there’s no alternative for ephemeral contracts), the account charge should be refilled when no state was created, in the current setup, there will be a x5 increase in gas costs for this type of transactions <shemnon> I think this cost is intentional. The only reason same tx self destruct was kept for backwards compatibility. So the 5x cost was viewed as a feature to discourage use. We should keep in mind some things are overcosted to discourage use, and that is a lever we should keep ready as a tool for things we need to get rid of. <milonite> re: **@shemnon** > I think this cost is intentional. The only reason same tx self destruct was kept for backwards compatibility. So the 5x cost was viewed as a feature to discourage use. We should keep in mind some things are overcosted to discourage use, and that is a lever we should keep ready as a tool for things we need to get rid of. Not sure if I follow why this would discourage the usage, would almost do the opposite as you are not encouraged to destroy the contract. Also, we are discouraging a legit use case. If it's actually intentionally doing so, it'd be good to pair it with a discussion of what ephemeral contracts should use instead <chfast> <@372317178906542081> there is a thread in ACD. https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1540737956929736766 <chfast> For me this is fixable, you just need to gather a big enough complaining group. <milonite> cool, llm are not good at finding discord discussions yet

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<milonite> Is there any discussion ongoing re refills for selfdestruct? 

As long as same-tx `SELFDESTRUCT` stays in the EVM (and there’s no alternative for ephemeral contracts), the account charge should be refilled when no state was created, in the current setup, there will be a x5 increase in gas costs for this type of transactions

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<shemnon> I think this cost is intentional. The only reason same tx self destruct was kept for backwards compatibility.  So the 5x cost was viewed as a feature to discourage use.

We should keep in mind some things are overcosted to discourage use, and that is a lever we should keep ready as a tool for things we need to get rid of.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<milonite> re: **@shemnon**
> I think this cost is intentional. The only reason same tx self destruct was kept for backwards compatibility.  So the 5x cost was viewed as a feature to discourage use.

We should keep in mind some things are overcosted to discourage use, and that is a lever we should keep ready as a tool for things we need to get rid of.
Not sure if I follow why this would discourage the usage, would almost do the opposite as you are not encouraged to destroy the contract. 

Also, we are discouraging a legit use case.
If it's actually intentionally doing so, it'd be good to pair it with a discussion of what ephemeral contracts should use instead
